items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: Raymond Ricker teaches there, I’m trying to think.

ctx.x: This was playing in nines and sevens and it was sort of — this guy was a Polish guy, Stan Kosky, it’s hard to remember his name. And in Chicago I started playing on the north side, those kind of places, those kinds of gigs. And I met a guy named Kenny Elliott, who is now with Lou Rawls, has been with Lou Rawls for I don’t know, for a long time, but Kenny and I, and then I got involved with Earth Wind and Fire when Maurice White had left. He had been with Ramsey Lewis for like, the Ramsey Lewis Trio, and then he…

a university without walls. You were allowed to have a certain number of instructors that could teach you things that you wanted to learn but they did not have to be a part of the university structure. So I was able to really study serious in-depth composition with Muhal Richard Abrams, which was a great composer, and get college credit for it. So everything was kind of working. And then the band performed at the Notre Dame Intercollegiate Jazz Festival, which all the schools, North Texas State, Richmond,…
